Note::RegexAccessor::split¶

Back to Note Regex Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

TokenBatch Note::RegexAccessor::split(std::string_view pattern,
                                    std::int64_t limit = -1) const

Cut Each Cell At Pattern Matches¶

split(pattern) treats every non-overlapping match as a delimiter and returns the text between delimiters. This is appropriate when the separator has a shape rather than one exact spelling: mixed comma/semicolon fields, variable whitespace, or decorated boundaries. Use Note::split(delimiter) when the delimiter is literal; it avoids regular-expression compilation and makes metacharacters ordinary text.

The pattern uses ECMAScript regular-expression syntax. Delimiter matches are consumed and do not appear in the result. Text before the first match and after the last match is retained. Adjacent matches preserve the empty field between them, and a cell with no match contributes the complete cell as one piece.

The limit Contract¶

limit counts splits, not returned pieces.

Value

Behavior

Negative, including the default -1

Split at every match

0

Do not split; emit each complete cell once

Positive n

Perform at most n splits per cell, leaving the remainder intact

The limit is applied independently to every source cell. With limit = 1, a two-cell Note can therefore produce up to four pieces, two from each cell.

Shape And Ownership¶

The result is ragged, so it cannot preserve the receiver’s rectangular shape as one Note. tokens() contains every piece in row-major cell order. offsets() is an Int64 Note of length source.numel() + 1; source cell i owns token indices in [offsets[i], offsets[i + 1]). Both Notes own their storage and remain valid after the temporary accessor and TokenBatch handle are destroyed.

Text input is required. Bytes, Bool, Int64, Float64, and undefined receivers are rejected. A malformed pattern is rejected before any cell result is published.

Example 1: Unlimited Splitting Preserves Empty Pieces¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({"A1,b22,,C333", "none"});
const auto pieces = source.regex().split(",");

std::cout << pluss::note::print(pieces.tokens()) << '\n';
std::cout << "offsets=[";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < pieces.offsets().integers().size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i == 0 ? "" : ", ") << pieces.offsets().integers()[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[5], dim=1, numel=5, encoding=utf8)
["A1", "b22", "", "C333", "none"]
offsets=[0, 4, 5]

The adjacent commas create the empty third piece. The second cell contains no comma and therefore contributes one unchanged piece.

Example 2: Limit One Leaves The Remaining Text Intact¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({"A1,b22,,C333", "none"});
const auto pieces = source.regex().split(",", 1);

std::cout << pluss::note::print(pieces.tokens()) << '\n';
std::cout << "offsets=[";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < pieces.offsets().integers().size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i == 0 ? "" : ", ") << pieces.offsets().integers()[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["A1", "b22,,C333", "none"]
offsets=[0, 2, 3]

Only the first comma in each cell can split. The unmatched remainder is not rescanned or discarded.

Example 3: Zero Disables Splitting¶

const auto pieces =
    pluss::make_note({"a,b", "c;d"}).regex().split(R"([,;])", 0);
std::cout << pluss::note::print(pieces.tokens()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["a,b", "c;d"]

limit = 0 is useful when a configurable pipeline must preserve the same call shape while temporarily disabling segmentation.

Example 4: A Pattern Can Recognize Several Delimiters¶

const auto pieces =
    pluss::make_note({"north, south;east"}).regex().split(R"(\s*[,;]\s*)");
std::cout << pluss::note::print(pieces.tokens()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["north", "south", "east"]

Including surrounding whitespace in the delimiter pattern removes it as part of the split. split() does not otherwise trim pieces.

Example 5: Malformed Patterns Fail Before A Result Escapes¶

try {
  (void)pluss::make_note({"a,b"}).regex().split("(");
} catch (const pluss::Error& error) {
  const std::string message(error.what());
  std::cout << message.substr(0, message.find('\n')) << '\n';
}

Output¶

regex().split: The expression contained mismatched ( and ).
